article_title: Is project-based learning effective among kindergarten and elementary students? A systematic review.
citation: Ferrero Marta, Vadillo Miguel A., León Samuel P. (2021). Is project-based learning effective among kindergarten and elementary students? A systematic review. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0249627
title: PjBL as a student-centred inquiry approach defined by key elements: driving problem, final product, group work, student empowerment, teacher guidance, and adapted evaluation tools
description: The review characterizes PjBL (used to cover both project- and problem-based learning) as "active, student-centred methods of instruction that encourage students to work in collaborative groups on real-world questions or challenges" with teachers as facilitators. Its central elements are a problem driving the activities, a final artifact or product, group work, student empowerment, teacher-provided guidance and resources, and evaluation tools adapted to PjBL such as notebook entries or portfolios. The review built a 30-item scale from these principles to assess prerequisites and fidelity.
requirements: An intervention faithful to the PjBL approach should include all its essential components as defined in the literature
constraints: PjBL and PBL are often employed interchangeably among researchers and teachers due to difficulties in distinguishing or defining their key features
examples: The review coded each included study against the key elements using a 30-item scale divided into prerequisites (Part A) and intervention fidelity (Part B)
